questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An equilibrium mixture taken in 2litre vessel of the reaction: $2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$ has 4 moles of $\text{SO}_2$, 3moles of $\text{O}_2$ and 6moles of $\text{SO}_3$ then the value of equilibrium constant $(K_c)$ will be:
questions.solution:
The given equilibrium reaction is:

$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$

The volume of the vessel is $V = 2$ L.

The equilibrium concentrations of the gases are:

$[\text{SO}_2] = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

$[\text{O}_2] = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

$[\text{SO}_3] = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

The expression for the equilibrium constant $K_c$ is:

$K_c = \dfrac{[\text{SO}_3]^2}{[\text{SO}_2]^2 [\text{O}_2]}$

Substituting the equilibrium concentrations into the expression:

$K_c = \dfrac{(3)^2}{(2)^2 \times (1.5)}$

$K_c = \dfrac{9}{4 \times 1.5} = \dfrac{9}{6} = 1.5 \text{ L mol}^{-1}$

Answer: 1.5 L mol$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the gaseous equilibrium
$2\text{AB}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{AB}_{(g)} + \text{B}_{2(g)}$
The expression relating the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) and equilibrium constant ($K_p$) and total pressure P is:
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\text{AB}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{AB}_{(g)} + \text{B}_{2(g)}$

Let the initial moles of $\text{AB}_2$ be $2$.

Moles at equilibrium:
$\text{AB}_2 = 2(1-\alpha)$
$\text{AB} = 2\alpha$
$\text{B}_2 = \alpha$

Total moles at equilibrium $= 2(1-\alpha) + 2\alpha + \alpha = 2 + \alpha$

Partial pressures at equilibrium:
$P_{\text{AB}_2} = \dfrac{2(1-\alpha)}{2+\alpha}P$
$P_{\text{AB}} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{2+\alpha}P$
$P_{\text{B}_2} = \dfrac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}P$

The equilibrium constant $K_p$ is given by:
$K_p = \dfrac{(P_{\text{AB}})^2 P_{\text{B}_2}}{(P_{\text{AB}_2})^2}$

Substituting the partial pressures:
$K_p = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{2+\alpha}P\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}P\right)}{\left(\dfrac{2(1-\alpha)}{2+\alpha}P\right)^2}$

$K_p = \dfrac{4\alpha^2 P^2}{(2+\alpha)^2} \times \dfrac{\alpha P}{2+\alpha} \times \dfrac{(2+\alpha)^2}{4(1-\alpha)^2 P^2}$

$K_p = \dfrac{\alpha^3 P}{(2+\alpha)(1-\alpha)^2}$

Assuming $\alpha$ is very small ($\alpha \ll 1$), we can approximate $2+\alpha \approx 2$ and $1-\alpha \approx 1$.

$K_p = \dfrac{\alpha^3 P}{2}$

$\alpha^3 = \dfrac{2K_p}{P}$

$\alpha = \left(\dfrac{2K_p}{P}\right)^{1/3}$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{2K_p}{P}\right)^{1/3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
If the equilibrium constant for $\text{N}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_{(g)}$ is 49
The equilibrium constant for the reaction $\text{NO}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \dfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2(g)}$ is __________
questions.solution:
For the given reaction $\text{N}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_{(g)}$, the equilibrium constant is $K_1 = 49$.

The required reaction is $\text{NO}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \dfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2(g)}$.

This reaction is obtained by reversing the given reaction and multiplying the stoichiometric coefficients by $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

The new equilibrium constant $K_2$ is related to $K_1$ as:

$K_2 = (K_1)^{-\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K_1}}$

Substituting the value of $K_1$:

$K_2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{49}} = \dfrac{1}{7} \approx 0.143$

Answer: $0.143$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a reaction
$2 A \rightleftharpoons 2 B+C$
2.0 moles of $A$ was placed in a one litre flask and the concentration of $B$ at equilibrium was found to be $0.4 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$. The equilibrium constant at $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is $\qquad\times 10^{-4}$
questions.solution:
The reaction is $2A \rightleftharpoons 2B + C$.

Initial moles: $[A]_0 = 2.0 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, $[B]_0 = 0$, $[C]_0 = 0$.

At equilibrium, let the concentration of $B$ be $0.4 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, if $2x$ moles of $B$ are formed, then $x$ moles of $C$ are formed and $2x$ moles of $A$ are consumed.

Given $[B]_{eq} = 2x = 0.4$, so $x = 0.2 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$.

Equilibrium concentrations are:
$[A]_{eq} = 2.0 - 2x = 2.0 - 0.4 = 1.6 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$
$[B]_{eq} = 0.4 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$
$[C]_{eq} = x = 0.2 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is given by:
$K_c = \dfrac{[B]^2 [C]}{[A]^2}$

$K_c = \dfrac{(0.4)^2 \times (0.2)}{(1.6)^2}$

$K_c = \dfrac{0.16 \times 0.2}{2.56} = \dfrac{0.032}{2.56}$

$K_c = \dfrac{32 \times 10^{-3}}{2560 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{32}{2560} = \dfrac{1}{80} = 0.0125$

$K_c = 125 \times 10^{-4}$

Answer: 125

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction $\mathrm{P}+\mathrm{Q} \leftrightharpoons \mathrm{R}+\mathrm{S}$, carried out at 298 K , the equilibrium constant was found to be 169 and the initial concentrations of all reactants and products was 1.0 M . What is the equilibrium concentration of the reactants?
questions.solution:
The reaction is $\mathrm{P} + \mathrm{Q} \leftrightharpoons \mathrm{R} + \mathrm{S}$. The equilibrium constant $K_c = 169$.

Initial concentrations are $[P]_0 = 1.0 \text{ M}$, $[Q]_0 = 1.0 \text{ M}$, $[R]_0 = 1.0 \text{ M}$, $[S]_0 = 1.0 \text{ M}$.

Let $x$ be the change in concentration at equilibrium. Since the reaction quotient $Q_c = \dfrac{[R][S]}{[P][Q]} = \dfrac{1 \times 1}{1 \times 1} = 1 \lt K_c = 169$, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction.

At equilibrium:
$[P] = 1 - x$
$[Q] = 1 - x$
$[R] = 1 + x$
$[S] = 1 + x$

The equilibrium constant expression is $K_c = \dfrac{[R][S]}{[P][Q]} = \dfrac{(1+x)^2}{(1-x)^2} = 169$.

Taking the square root of both sides:
$\dfrac{1+x}{1-x} = \sqrt{169} = 13$.

$1 + x = 13(1 - x)$
$1 + x = 13 - 13x$
$14x = 12$
$x = \dfrac{12}{14} = \dfrac{6}{7} \approx 0.857$.

The equilibrium concentration of the reactants $[P] = [Q] = 1 - x = 1 - 0.857 = 0.143 \text{ M}$.

Answer: 0.143 M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the reaction
$\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{~s})+3 \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{l})+3 \mathrm{CQ}_2(\mathrm{~g})$
In accordance with Le-Chatlier's principle, which of the following will not disturbs the equilibrium?
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{s}) + 3 \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{l}) + 3 \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$.

According to Le-Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium position of a reaction is affected by changes in the concentration of species that are in the gaseous or aqueous phase. Species in the solid or liquid phase have a constant activity (or concentration) and their addition or removal does not change the reaction quotient $Q_c$ or the equilibrium constant $K_c$.

In the given reaction, $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ is in the solid state (s). Therefore, changing the amount of $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ does not shift the equilibrium position.

The species $\mathrm{CO}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ are in the gaseous phase (g), so changing their concentrations will disturb the equilibrium.

Answer: Addition of $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a reaction,
$A+B \rightleftharpoons 2 C$
1.0 mole of $A, 1.5$ mole of $B$ and 0.5 mole of $C$ were taken in a 1 L vessel. At equilibrium, the concentration of $C$ was $1.0 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$. The equilibrium constant for the reaction is $x / 15$. The value of ' $x$ ' is:
questions.solution:
The reaction is $A + B \rightleftharpoons 2C$.

Initial moles:
$[A]_0 = 1.0 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$
$[B]_0 = 1.5 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$
$[C]_0 = 0.5 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Let the change in concentration of $A$ be $-y$. Then the change in $B$ is $-y$ and the change in $C$ is $+2y$.

At equilibrium:
$[A]_{eq} = 1.0 - y$
$[B]_{eq} = 1.5 - y$
$[C]_{eq} = 0.5 + 2y$

Given $[C]_{eq} = 1.0 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, we have:
$0.5 + 2y = 1.0 \Rightarrow 2y = 0.5 \Rightarrow y = 0.25$.

Calculating equilibrium concentrations:
$[A]_{eq} = 1.0 - 0.25 = 0.75 = \dfrac{3}{4}$
$[B]_{eq} = 1.5 - 0.25 = 1.25 = \dfrac{5}{4}$
$[C]_{eq} = 1.0$

The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is given by:
$K_c = \dfrac{[C]^2}{[A][B]} = \dfrac{(1.0)^2}{(0.75)(1.25)} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{5}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{15}{16}} = \dfrac{16}{15}$.

Given $K_c = \dfrac{x}{15}$, we have $\dfrac{x}{15} = \dfrac{16}{15}$, which implies $x = 16$.

Answer: $16$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the equilibrium, $2 \mathrm{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{~N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2$, 6 mol of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is taken in 10 L flask. If concentration of $\mathrm{N}_2$ at equilibrium is $x$, then concentration of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ at equilibrium is
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{lccc} & 2 \mathrm{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons & \mathrm{~N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \\ \\ \text{Initial} & \frac{6}{\mathrm{~mol}} \mathrm{~mol} & 0 & 0 \\ \\ \text{concentration} & 10 & & \\ \\ & =0.6 \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L} & & \\ \\ \begin{array}{l} \text{Concentration} \\ \\ \text{at equilibrium}\end{array} & 0.6-2 x & x & 3 x\end{array}$ \\ When $x$ moles of $\mathrm{N}_2$ are formed, $3 x$ moles of $\mathrm{H}_2$ will formed and $2 x$ moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ would react (according to balance equation).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The equilibrium constant of given reaction is 100 .
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}_2$ (gas)
What is the equilibrium constant for the reaction given below?
$\mathrm{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~N}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{N}_2+2 \mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}_2 ; k=100$...(i)
To find equilibrium constant of
$\mathrm{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~N}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$...(ii)
If we divide eq (i) by 2 and taking the reverse we will obtain equation (ii).
$\begin{aligned} \\ \text { Required } k & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{100}}=\frac{1}{10}=0.1 \\ \\ k & =0.1 \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text{S}_8$ on heating at a temperature above 1000 K, changes to $\text{S}_2(g)$. When $\text{S}_8$ is heated above 1000 K at an initial pressure of 1 atm, the partial pressure of $\text{S}_8$ falls by 32% at equilibrium. The equilibrium constant for the conversion is:
questions.solution:
$S_8(g) \rightleftharpoons 4S_2(g)$

Initial pressure of $S_8 = 1$ atm. Pressure falls by 32%:
$P_{S_8} = 1 - 0.32 = 0.68$ atm
$P_{S_2} = 4 \times 0.32 = 1.28$ atm

$K_p = \dfrac{(P_{S_2})^4}{P_{S_8}} = \dfrac{(1.28)^4}{0.68} = \dfrac{2.684}{0.68} \approx 3.94$ atm$^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
At $700\text{ K}$, the Equilibrium constant value for the formation of HI from $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$ is $49.0$.
$0.7\text{ mole}$ of $\text{HI(g)}$ is present at equilibrium. What will be the concentrations of $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$ gases if we initially started with $\text{HI(g)}$ and allowed the reaction to reach equilibrium at the same temperature?
questions.solution:
The reaction is: $H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$

$K_c = \dfrac{[HI]^2}{[H_2][I_2]} = 49.0$

Since the reaction starts with only $HI(g)$, it decomposes to give $H_2$ and $I_2$ in 1:1 ratio.
Let $[H_2] = [I_2] = x$

$49.0 = \dfrac{(0.7)^2}{x^2}$

$x^2 = \dfrac{0.49}{49.0} = 0.01$

$x = 0.1$ mol/L

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following equilibrium,
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 \mathrm{No}(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 ; K_{\mathrm{G}_1}=2.4 \times 10^{20} \\
& \mathrm{No}(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Br}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NoBr}(g) ; K_{C_2}=1.4
\end{aligned}$
Calculate $K_C$ for the reaction,
$\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~N}_2(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NOBr}(g)$
questions.solution:
For, $2 \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2+\mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}_1}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{[\mathrm{NO}]^2}=2.4 \times 10^{20}$
For,
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { For, } \mathrm{NO}(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NOBr}(g) \\
& K_{C_2}=\frac{[\mathrm{NOBr}]}{[\mathrm{NO}]\left[\mathrm{Br}_2\right]^{1 / 2}}=1.4 \\
& \text { and } K_C=\frac{[\mathrm{NOBr}]}{\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]^{1 / 2}\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{1 / 2}\left[\mathrm{Br}_2\right]^{1 / 2}} \\
& \text { or } K_C=\sqrt{\frac{1}{K_{\mathrm{C}_1}}} \times K_{C_2}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{2.4 \times 10^{20}}} \times 1.4 \\
& K_C=8.96 \times 10^{-11}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The equilibrium constants for the reactions $a, b$, and $c$ are as given:
a) $\mathrm{N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2=2 \mathrm{NH}_3: \mathrm{K}_1$
b) $\mathrm{N}_2+\mathrm{O}_2=2 \mathrm{NO}: \mathrm{K}_2$
c) $2 \mathrm{H}_2+\mathrm{O}_2=2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}: \mathrm{K}_3$
What would be the Equilibrium constant for the reaction:
$4 \mathrm{NH}_3+5 \mathrm{O}_2=4 \mathrm{NO}+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} ; \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{x}}$
questions.solution:
The given reactions are:
a) $\mathrm{N}_2 + 3\mathrm{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3$ with equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_1$
b) $\mathrm{N}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}$ with equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_2$
c) $2\mathrm{H}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ with equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_3$

The target reaction is $4\mathrm{NH}_3 + 5\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 4\mathrm{NO} + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

To obtain the target reaction, we manipulate the given equations:
1. Reverse reaction (a) and multiply by 2: $4\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{N}_2 + 6\mathrm{H}_2$. The equilibrium constant becomes $\left(\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{K}_1}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{K}_1^2}$.
2. Keep reaction (b) as is and multiply by 2: $2\mathrm{N}_2 + 2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 4\mathrm{NO}$. The equilibrium constant becomes $\mathrm{K}_2^2$.
3. Multiply reaction (c) by 3: $6\mathrm{H}_2 + 3\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. The equilibrium constant becomes $\mathrm{K}_3^3$.

Adding these three modified reactions:
$(4\mathrm{NH}_3) + (2\mathrm{N}_2 + 2\mathrm{O}_2) + (6\mathrm{H}_2 + 3\mathrm{O}_2) \rightleftharpoons (2\mathrm{N}_2 + 6\mathrm{H}_2) + (4\mathrm{NO}) + (6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})$

Canceling common species ($2\mathrm{N}_2$ and $6\mathrm{H}_2$) on both sides gives:
$4\mathrm{NH}_3 + 5\mathrm{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 4\mathrm{NO} + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$

The equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_x$ is the product of the constants of the modified reactions:
$\mathrm{K}_x = \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{K}_1^2} \times \mathrm{K}_2^2 \times \mathrm{K}_3^3 = \dfrac{\mathrm{K}_2^2 \mathrm{K}_3^3}{\mathrm{K}_1^2}$

Answer: $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{K}_2{ }^2 \mathrm{~K}_3{ }^3 / \mathrm{K}_1{ }^2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following equilibrium,
$2\text{NO}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g); K_{C_1} = 2.4 \times 10^{20}\text{NO}(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{Br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{NOBr}(g); K_{C_2} = 1.4$
Calculate $K_C$ for the reaction,
$\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{Br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{NOBr}(g)$
questions.solution:
Target reaction: $\dfrac{1}{2}N_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}Br_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NOBr(g)$

Reverse reaction 1 and multiply by $\dfrac{1}{2}$:
$\dfrac{1}{2}N_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NO(g)$, $K'' = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K_1}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2.4 \times 10^{20}}}$

Add reaction 2 as it is:
$NO(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}Br_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NOBr(g)$, $K_2 = 1.4$

$K_C = K'' \times K_2 = \dfrac{1.4}{\sqrt{2.4 \times 10^{20}}} = \dfrac{1.4}{\sqrt{2.4} \times 10^{10}}$

$= \dfrac{1.4 \times 0.64}{10^{10}} \approx \dfrac{0.896}{10^{10}} = 8.96 \times 10^{-11}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction, $\mathrm{H}_2(g)+\mathrm{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{HI}(g)$ the position of equilibrium can be shifted to the right by
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $\mathrm{H}_2(g) + \mathrm{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{HI}(g)$. According to Le Chatelier's principle, the position of equilibrium shifts in a direction that counteracts the change applied to the system.

Adding a reactant, such as $\mathrm{I}_2(g)$ or $\mathrm{H}_2(g)$, increases the concentration of the reactants. To restore equilibrium, the system shifts to the right, consuming the added reactant and producing more product $\mathrm{HI}(g)$.

Addition of $\mathrm{HI}$ would increase the product concentration, shifting the equilibrium to the left. Increasing the temperature for this specific reaction (which is nearly thermoneutral) has a negligible effect compared to concentration changes, and the reaction is not significantly endothermic or exothermic to favor the right side solely by temperature increase. Therefore, the addition of $\mathrm{I}_2$ is the correct method to shift the equilibrium to the right.

Answer: addition of $\mathrm{I}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The equilibrium constant, $K_C$ for $3 \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6(\mathrm{~g})$ is $4 \mathrm{~L}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-2}$. If the equilil rium concentration of benzene is $0.5 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ than what is the value of concentration of ethylene?
questions.solution:
The chemical equation for the reaction is $3 \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{6}(\mathrm{g})$.

The expression for the equilibrium constant $K_{C}$ is given by:

$K_{C} = \dfrac{[\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{6}]}{[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}]^{3}}$

Given $K_{C} = 4 \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-2}$ and $[\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{6}] = 0.5 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$.

Substituting the values into the expression:

$4 = \dfrac{0.5}{[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}]^{3}}$

$[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}]^{3} = \dfrac{0.5}{4} = 0.125$

$[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}] = (0.125)^{1/3} = (0.5^{3})^{1/3} = 0.5 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$.

Answer: $0.5 \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction $2 \mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5 \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2$. If inital pressure is $100 \mathrm{~atm}$ and rate constant $k$ is $3.38 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. After $20 \mathrm{~min}$ the final pressure of $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ will be
questions.solution:
The reaction $2 \mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5 \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2$ is a first-order reaction. The rate equation for a first-order reaction is given by $P_t = P_0 e^{-kt}$, where $P_0$ is the initial pressure and $P_t$ is the pressure at time $t$.

Given values are:
$P_0 = 100 \text{ atm}$
$k = 3.38 \times 10^{-5} \text{ s}^{-1}$
$t = 20 \text{ min} = 20 \times 60 \text{ s} = 1200 \text{ s}$

Substituting these values into the equation:
$P_t = 100 \times e^{-(3.38 \times 10^{-5}) \times 1200}$

Calculate the exponent:
$-(3.38 \times 10^{-5}) \times 1200 = -0.04056$

Now calculate $P_t$:
$P_t = 100 \times e^{-0.04056}$
Using the approximation $e^{-x} \approx 1 - x$ for small $x$:
$P_t \approx 100 \times (1 - 0.04056) = 100 \times 0.95944 = 95.944 \text{ atm}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $96 \text{ atm}$.

Answer: $96 \mathrm{~atm}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the equilibrium, $A B \rightleftharpoons A+B$, if the equilibrium concentration of $A$ is double, then equilibrium concentration of $B$ will be
questions.solution:
For the equilibrium reaction $AB \rightleftharpoons A + B$, the equilibrium constant $K_{eq}$ is given by the expression:

$K_{eq} = \dfrac{[A][B]}{[AB]}$

Since $K_{eq}$ is a constant at a fixed temperature, the product of the concentrations of the products divided by the concentration of the reactant remains constant. Let the initial equilibrium concentrations be $[A]_1$, $[B]_1$, and $[AB]_1$. Then $K_{eq} = \dfrac{[A]_1 [B]_1}{[AB]_1}$.

If the equilibrium concentration of $A$ is doubled, let the new concentration be $[A]_2 = 2[A]_1$. Assuming the concentration of the reactant $[AB]$ remains effectively constant or the system adjusts such that the ratio is maintained, we have:

$\dfrac{[A]_1 [B]_1}{[AB]} = \dfrac{[A]_2 [B]_2}{[AB]}$

$[A]_1 [B]_1 = (2[A]_1) [B]_2$

$[B]_2 = \dfrac{[A]_1 [B]_1}{2[A]_1} = \dfrac{1}{2} [B]_1$

Therefore, the equilibrium concentration of $B$ becomes half of its original value.

Answer: half

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the equilibrium, $2 \mathrm{NOCl}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}(g)+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(g)$, the value of the equilibrium constant, $K_{C}$ is $3.75 \times 10^{-6}$ at $1069 \mathrm{~K}$. The value of $K_{p}$ for the reaction at this temperature will be
questions.solution:
The relationship between the equilibrium constants $K_{p}$ and $K_{c}$ is given by the equation $K_{p} = K_{c}(RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$.

For the reaction $2 \mathrm{NOCl}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}(g) + \mathrm{Cl}_{2}(g)$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is calculated as $\Delta n_{g} = (2 + 1) - 2 = 1$.

Given values are $K_{c} = 3.75 \times 10^{-6}$, $R = 0.0821 \text{ L atm K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, and $T = 1069 \text{ K}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$K_{p} = (3.75 \times 10^{-6}) \times (0.0821 \times 1069)^{1}$

$K_{p} = 3.75 \times 10^{-6} \times 87.7649$

$K_{p} \approx 0.000329118$

Rounding to the appropriate precision, $K_{p} \approx 0.00033$.

Answer: $0.00033$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The value of $\Delta G^{\circ}$ for the phosphorylation of glucose in glycolysis is $13.8 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$. The value of $K_{C}$ at $298 \mathrm{~K}$ is
questions.solution:
The relationship between the standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^{\circ}$ and the equilibrium constant $K_{C}$ is given by the equation $\Delta G^{\circ} = -RT \ln K_{C}$.

Given values are $\Delta G^{\circ} = 13.8 \text{ kJ/mol} = 13800 \text{ J/mol}$, $R = 8.314 \text{ J/(mol K)}$, and $T = 298 \text{ K}$.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$13800 = -(8.314) \times (298) \times \ln K_{C}$

$\ln K_{C} = -\dfrac{13800}{8.314 \times 298}$

$\ln K_{C} = -\dfrac{13800}{2477.572} \approx -5.570$

$K_{C} = e^{-5.570}$

$K_{C} \approx 3.81 \times 10^{-3}$

Answer: $3.81 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical equilibrium of a reversible reaction is not influenced by
questions.solution: The chemical equilibrium of a reversible reaction is not influenced by catalyst as it only increase the rate of reaction to achieve the equilibrium faster. The increase in rate of forward direction is equal to increase in rate of backward direction at equilibrium. $\therefore$ Equilibrium point is not shifted.

questions.q: The gaseous reaction $A+B \rightleftharpoons 2 C+D+Q$ is most favoured at
questions.solution:
For the reaction

A+B \rightleftharpoons 2 C+D+Q

As the reaction is exothermic, low temperature favours formed direction according to Le-Chatelier's principle. Also $\Delta n_{(g)}=(2+1)-(1+1)=1\begin{aligned} \because \quad \Delta n_{\mathrm{g}}=&+\text { ve } \\ & \text { (low pressure favours forward direction) } \end{aligned}\therefore$ Low pressure and temperature favours formed direction for the reaction.

If $\Delta n$ is positive than $K_{p}\gt K_{C}$ also, gaseous moles of product > moles of reactant.
$\therefore$ Forward reaction is favoured by low pressure, according to Le-Chatelier's principle.
